english: Father, a young man (mógʰus) stole our pig. He who steals is evil-minded. Did anyone see him? The gods saw him and are angry. Son, do not steal. I do not steal.
uncertain: súHm̥ read as 'pig' (acc of *suH-); could be meant as something else

english: Where, brother, do you swim? In the water at (on) the lake, with the children, for your youthfulness(?). I was afraid. Do not tremble; I held/bore you. Look, I swim. Soon you will learn.
uncertain: toy Hyowdʰéye unclear: dative of a 'youth/joint' noun?

english: What, father, is fire? Agni is a god. He warms our house and at night protects/heats us. What did my child learn? Grasp it(?). Son, do not touch the fire. I do not touch it.
uncertain: h₁íd h₁éps — 'you grasped it'? reads as a non-answer to the question
who asks 'what did my child learn'

english: What do you do in the field? I plough the field. What do you plough? You make the earth yield and we eat. Let us plough together. Son, you are young. When you grow, you will plough.
uncertain: dʰéwgʰesi 'you make yield/milk' — 2sg subject odd if the father ploughs

english: Someone is coming. What shall I say to him? Say to him: 'Dear guest, come.' Dear guest, come. Now give him water and set him by the fire on a seat. Now what did I say? You said it. Be dear to us.
uncertain: last line n̥sméy priHós h₁sdʰí 'be dear to us'

english: Who, mother, is Dyēus? Dyēus is a great king. Father Dyēus sees us. Does he see me? He sees you. Do not deceive anyone. I deceive no one. Now may he protect you, daughter.
